intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes
experiences.description: Enjoy world-class skiing across 213km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels. Families can take advantage of dedicated beginner slopes and ski schools offering lessons for children and adults. The breathtaking alpine scenery and well-maintained runs make this a quintessential Swiss Alps experience.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express for a panoramic journey through dramatic alpine landscapes, frozen valleys, and snow-capped peaks. This family-friendly rail experience covers stunning viaducts and tunnels, offering an unforgettable window into the Swiss Alps without strenuous physical activity.

experiences.name: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore serene snow-covered forests and alpine meadows on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trails are designed for all ages and fitness levels, with guides sharing local wildlife knowledge and mountain ecology. A magical way to experience the quieter side of the Alps away from ski crowds.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Participate in a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class at a traditional alpine chalet, learning about centuries-old Swiss cheese-making traditions. Families enjoy melting local Gruyère and Emmental cheeses while tasting regional breads, meats, and Swiss wines or hot chocolate for kids.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, descending through pine forests and open alpine terrain on traditional wooden sleds. The run is well-lit for evening sessions and suitable for children aged 5 and up, making it a highlight activity for families seeking fun winter thrills.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, descending through pine forests and open alpine terrain on traditional wooden sleds. The run is well-lit for evening sessions and suitable for children aged 5 and up, making it a highlight activity for families seeking fun winter thrills.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Transit — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities. Use this time to rest on the plane.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the train from Zurich HB to Grindelwald via Interlaken Ost (approx. 2.5–3 hrs, book in advance with a Swiss Travel Pass for savings). Check in to your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen. Take a relaxed stroll through Grindelwald village, get oriented, and pick up a Jungfrau ski region map from the tourist office. Browse the village shops and admire the iconic Eiger North Face backdrop.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your accommodation. Head to a local casual eatery for a welcome dinner in Grindelwald village. Rest early to recover from travel and prepare for an active week.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a quick snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 5–10 for a sandwich or pastry).
meals.lunch: Grab a takeaway sandwich or pretzel at the train station in Interlaken Ost during your transit (CHF 6–10).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or Café 3692 in Grindelwald — try the budget-friendly daily special (Tagesmenü) which typically includes soup, main, and dessert for CHF 18–25. Alternatively, pick up groceries from the local Migros or Coop supermarket for a self-catered dinner (CHF 10–15).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Swiss Travel Pass or Jungfrau Travel Pass before or upon arrival to save significantly on train and lift costs throughout the week. Stock up on snacks and breakfast items at Coop or Migros supermarket in Grindelwald to reduce meal costs. Confirm accommodation check-in time in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Beginner/Family Ski Day at Grindelwald First Ski Area — Head to the First gondola (short walk or bus from village). The First ski area offers excellent beginner and intermediate slopes perfect for families. Rent ski equipment from one of the village rental shops (book ahead online for discounts — budget CHF 35–45/day for skis, boots, poles). Purchase a half-day or full-day lift pass for Grindelwald First (cheaper than the full Jungfrau region pass for a first trial day — approx. CHF 55–65 for adults, less for children).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing at Grindelwald First or, if legs are tired, try the First Flieger zip line or First Flyer (included with some passes or CHF 20–25 extra) — a thrilling family-friendly experience. Alternatively, take a scenic gondola ride up to First (2,168m) and enjoy panoramic Alpine views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald village by 16:30. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a village café. Prepare a simple self-catered dinner at the accommodation using groceries from Coop or Migros.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation — bread, cheese, yogurt, and fruit purchased from Migros/Coop (CHF 3–5 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade lunch or buy a mountain hut soup and bread at the First mountain restaurant (Berghaus First) — budget CHF 12–16 for soup and a snack to keep costs low.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation — pasta, sauce, and salad from Migros (CHF 8–12 per person). Or try Restaurant Pizzeria Grindelwald for a budget pizza (CHF 18–22).

day_by_day.notes: Book ski rental equipment online at least 2–3 days in advance for 10–20% savings. Families with children under 9 ski free with a paying adult on the Jungfrau region pass. Dress in warm layers — temperatures at altitude can be -10°C or colder. Apply sunscreen even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run (Day Trip) — Take an early train from Grindelwald toward Chur/Maienfeld (approx. 2.5 hrs via Interlaken and Spiez — covered by Swiss Travel Pass). Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, descending through pine forests on the famous Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan track. Toboggan rental is available on-site (approx. CHF 10–15). The run is approximately 4 km long and suitable for families with children.
day_by_day.afternoon: After tobogganing, explore the charming village of Maienfeld, known as the setting for Heidi's story. Visit the Heidiland region and take a short walk to Heididorf (Heidi's village) — a fun and affordable family activity (entrance approx. CHF 8–10 for adults, CHF 5 for children). Head back by train toward Grindelwald in the mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Grindelwald by early evening. Relax tired legs with a warm bath or sauna if available at the boutique stay. Light self-catered dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast before departure — pack portable snacks (bananas, energy bars, thermos of hot tea) for the train journey.
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches and snacks from home or grab a quick meal at the Maienfeld village bakery or local café (CHF 8–14). Avoid mountain resort restaurants to save budget.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation — hearty soup or stew made from supermarket ingredients (CHF 8–12 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Check Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) timetable the evening before to plan the earliest practical train. The Swiss Travel Pass covers train travel to Maienfeld. Toboggan runs may be weather-dependent — check local conditions at www.flaescherberg.ch. Bring hand warmers for children.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Excursion (Morning Departure) — Take the cogwheel train from Grindelwald Grund station to Jungfraujoch (3,454m), the highest railway station in Europe. Book tickets in advance online for the 'Good Morning Ticket' (available before 07:30 departure) — significantly discounted at approx. CHF 145–155 per adult vs. CHF 220+ regular price. Children under 16 travel at reduced rates. Marvel at the Aletsch Glacier, the Sphinx Observatory, and 360° Alpine panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ice Palace (carved inside the glacier), the Plateau (for snowshoeing or short walks), and the Snow Fun Park at Jungfraujoch. Descend back to Grindelwald by early afternoon (plan to be back by 14:00–15:00). Stop at Kleine Scheidegg on the way back for a quick scenic break — no extra cost with your rail ticket.
day_by_day.evening: Rest at accommodation. This is the biggest expense day of the trip, so keep dinner costs minimal with self-catering.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast before 07:00 departure — pre-packed overnight oats or bread with peanut butter and a flask of coffee.
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch from the accommodation to eat at Jungfraujoch (the on-site restaurants are very expensive — CHF 25–40 per dish). Alternatively, budget CHF 15–20 for a simple soup at the Aletsch self-service restaurant if needed.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner — simple rice and vegetable stir-fry or canned soup with crusty bread from Migros (CHF 8–12 per person). Treat yourselves to a small Swiss chocolate bar as dessert!

day_by_day.notes: The 'Good Morning Ticket' discount is only available for the earliest departures — book weeks in advance as it sells out quickly. Dress extremely warmly: temperatures at Jungfraujoch can reach -20°C with wind chill. Altitude sickness is possible — ascend slowly and stay hydrated. Children under 6 should be kept warm and monitored closely.

day_by_day.morning: Skiing at Männlichen — Wengen Ski Area — Take the Wengen train from Grindelwald Grund (included in Jungfrau Travel Pass) up to Wengen, then the Männlichen gondola to the top. Enjoy the famous 'Royal Route' ski run from Männlichen to Grindelwald Grund — a long, scenic blue/red run suitable for intermediate families. Ski instructors are available for group lessons at Wengen Ski School (group lessons approx. CHF 45–55/half day — book ahead).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Lauberhorn area runs above Wengen — home to the famous World Cup Downhill course. Families can enjoy the easier parallel runs. Take a scenic break at a mid-mountain sun terrace and enjoy the views. Return to Grindelwald by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Grindelwald village at dusk. Visit the free outdoor ice rink in the village center (skate rental approx. CHF 5–8). Enjoy a fondue dinner as a special mid-trip treat.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast at accommodation.
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch or purchase a mountain soup and bread combo at a Wengen mountain restaurant (CHF 12–16). Look for 'Tagesmenü' (daily special) boards for the best value.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Gasthof Hirschen in Grindelwald — try their traditional Swiss cheese fondue (CHF 22–28 per person). This is a budget splurge but a must-do cultural experience. Share a pot between two people to reduce cost.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfrau Travel Pass (3-day or 5-day) covers the Wengen train, Männlichen gondola, and most lifts in the region — far better value than daily passes if you're skiing multiple days. Check if your boutique stay offers a guest card for additional discounts.

day_by_day.morning: Snowshoeing or Winter Hiking at Bachalpsee — Rent snowshoes in Grindelwald village (approx. CHF 15–20/day). Take the First gondola up and hike the spectacular trail to Bachalpsee (lake) — a 2.5 km easy snowshoe trail with stunning views of the Schreckhorn and Finsteraarhorn peaks. This is a free activity beyond the gondola cost (covered by Jungfrau Pass or CHF 28 one-way). Ideal for families with children aged 6+.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to First by early afternoon. Try the First Glider (hang glider-style ride) if budget allows (CHF 29 per person) — an unforgettable thrill for older children and adults. Alternatively, sled down from First on rented sleds (CHF 10–15 sled rental) on designated sled runs — a free, exhilarating alternative to skiing.
day_by_day.evening: Final big evening in Grindelwald. Visit the village Christmas/winter market stalls if operating. Enjoy a casual dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered breakfast — make it hearty with eggs, toast, and fruit before the snowshoe hike.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the snowshoe trail — thermos of hot soup, sandwiches, and chocolate. Eat with a view of the Alps (free and spectacular!).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Café 3692 or Espresso Bar in Grindelwald — try the Rösti (Swiss potato dish) with fried egg and salad (CHF 16–22). Budget-friendly and authentically Swiss.

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe trails are free to use once you reach the trailhead. Check trail conditions with the Grindelwald tourist office or at www.jungfrau.ch. Bring trekking poles if available for snowshoeing with children. Saturday may be busier on the mountain — start early to beat crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Final Morning in Grindelwald — Sleep in and enjoy a relaxed self-catered breakfast. Take a gentle final walk through Grindelwald village, browse local shops for affordable Swiss souvenirs (Swiss chocolate, postcards, small wooden ornaments). Visit the free Grindelwald Museum (kleine Museum) for a quick look at local Alpine history if time allows.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of accommodation (confirm check-out time with hotel). Pack bags and begin the return journey by train from Grindelwald toward Zurich or your onward destination. The scenic train ride through the Bernese Oberland is itself a highlight — enjoy the views one last time. Arrive in Zurich or departure city in the mid-to-late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Departure or overnight in Zurich if flight is the following day. If departing from Zurich Airport, allow 2+ hours before your flight for check-in and security.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast at accommodation — use up remaining groceries to minimize waste and cost.
meals.lunch: Grab a takeaway from the Coop or Migros at Interlaken Ost or Bern train station during transit (CHF 8–12 — excellent value Swiss supermarket hot food counters).
meals.dinner: If overnighting in Zurich: try Zeughauskeller in Zurich Altstadt — a historic beer hall with affordable Swiss classics like sausage and Rösti (CHF 20–28). If departing: airport food or pack remaining snacks.

day_by_day.notes: Keep all train tickets and Swiss Travel Pass handy for the return journey. Zurich Airport has excellent train connections directly from the terminal (ZRH Airport station). Allow extra time on Sundays as some train services run on reduced timetables. Consider buying a final Swiss chocolate bar at the airport duty-free as a budget-friendly gift — often cheaper than village shops.

trip_options.title: Classic Swiss Alps, Switzerland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Grindelwald is approximately 2.5–3 hours by train via Interlaken Ost.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Grindelwald-Wengen boutique hotel around 15:30–16:00. Check in, unpack, and settle into your alpine accommodation. Take a leisurely orientation stroll through Grindelwald village, admiring the iconic Eiger North Face views. Visit the local sport shop to rent ski equipment or purchase lift passes for the week ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby cozy restaurant in Grindelwald village. Explore the charming pedestrian streets, pick up snacks and supplies from a local Coop or Migros supermarket for the room.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport — grab a coffee and pastry at a Zurich/Geneva airport café such as Marché.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the train station in Interlaken Ost — try a Brezel pretzel and hot chocolate from the station kiosk (budget-friendly, ~CHF 10–12).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — a welcoming mid-range alpine restaurant offering Swiss classics like Rösti, Bratwurst, and local cheese dishes. Budget ~CHF 30–45 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book ski rental online (e.g., Intersport Grindelwald) to save 10–15% and avoid queues. Purchase the Jungfrau Ski Region multi-day lift pass at the hotel desk or online. Keep the first evening light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm hotel breakfast times for the next morning.

day_by_day.morning: First ski day on the Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes. Head to the Grindelwald-First gondola (5-minute walk from most village hotels) by 9:00 AM to beat crowds. The First ski area offers 45km of varied pistes — beginners and younger children can stick to the gentle blue runs near the top station, while stronger skiers tackle the red and black runs down toward Bort and Grindelwald. Ski school sessions for kids start at 9:30 AM (pre-book with Skischule Grindelwald).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing after a mid-mountain lunch break. Explore the Kleine Scheidegg area accessible via the Männlichen gondola from Grindelwald Grund — the panoramic runs here with views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau are unmissable. Gentler cruising pistes make this ideal for families skiing together. Wrap up by 15:30 to avoid icy afternoon conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Return ski gear to the rental shop if needed, then warm up with a Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate at a village café. Relax tired muscles before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — typically included or ~CHF 18–25 per person at boutique stays. Fuel up with muesli, eggs, cold cuts, and fresh bread.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Berghaus Bort mid-mountain — a classic ski hut serving hearty Älplermagronen (Swiss mac and cheese), soup, and hot drinks. Budget ~CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter in Grindelwald — popular for its wood-fired dishes and relaxed atmosphere. Try the Swiss beef burger or fondue starter. Budget ~CHF 35–50 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a 6-day Jungfrau Ski Region lift pass for best value (~CHF 330–360 for adults, ~CHF 165–180 for children aged 6–15 as of recent seasons — verify current pricing). Apply sunscreen even on cloudy days — alpine UV reflection off snow is intense. Helmets are strongly recommended and available at rental shops.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking guided tour. Meet your certified mountain guide at 9:00 AM near the Grindelwald tourist office. The guided route winds through snow-covered forests above the village toward the Pfingstegg area or along the Eiger Trail lower section — both suitable for families with children aged 6+. Snowshoe rental is included in most guided packages (~CHF 45–60 per adult, ~CHF 25–35 per child). Enjoy the peaceful silence of the winter forest, spot animal tracks, and learn about alpine ecology.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning to the village by 12:30, take the afternoon to visit the Grindelwald Sports Centre or enjoy free sledging on the beginner slope near First (sleds available to rent). Alternatively, visit the Grindelwald Ice Rink (Kunsteisbahn) for a fun family ice skating session — skate hire available on-site (~CHF 8–12 per person entry + skate rental).
day_by_day.evening: Warm up with a traditional Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — book an early evening fondue cooking class at a local alpine chalet or restaurant such as Chalet Egg. Learn to make authentic cheese fondue and raclette, then eat what you've prepared together as a family. A memorable and interactive cultural highlight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch prepared by the hotel or purchased the night before from Migros — sandwiches, fruit, and energy bars to eat during the snowshoe tour rest break.
meals.dinner: The fondue cooking class typically includes dinner as part of the experience (~CHF 55–75 per adult, ~CHF 30–40 per child). Includes bread, fondue, raclette, charcuterie, and local wine or juice.

day_by_day.notes: Book the snowshoeing guided tour and fondue cooking class at least 48 hours in advance — these fill up quickly in peak February season. Wear waterproof boots and warm layered clothing for snowshoeing. The fondue evening is a wonderful cultural moment — encourage children to try raclette even if hesitant!

day_by_day.morning: Full ski day focusing on the Wengen and Lauberhorn area. Take the train from Grindelwald to Kleine Scheidegg (covered by ski pass) and ski down toward Wengen on the famous Lauberhorn race piste — one of the most iconic descents in the world. The wide, well-groomed runs here are excellent for intermediate skiers and confident families. Consider a guided ski tour with a local instructor to discover hidden gems and improve technique (~CHF 70–90 per person for a half-day group lesson).
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Männlichen plateau area — take the Männlichen cable car from Wengen and enjoy the breathtaking 360-degree panoramic views of the Bernese Alps. The Royal Walk (a flat 30-minute scenic walk along the ridge) is accessible even in ski boots and offers unbeatable photo opportunities of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. Ski back down to Grindelwald Grund via the long, sweeping Männlichen-Grindelwald run (8km blue/red — a family favorite).
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski drinks at Bar 3692 or Espresso Bar in Grindelwald village. Relax, share photos from the day, and enjoy the lively but family-friendly village atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet.
meals.lunch: Restaurant Männlichen Summit — panoramic mountain restaurant with stunning views. Try the daily soup, Rösti with fried egg, or a hearty alpine platter. Budget ~CHF 25–35 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Mercado in Grindelwald — offers a broader European menu with Swiss touches, popular with families. Try the veal Zürich-style (Züri Geschnetzeltes) with Rösti. Budget ~CHF 35–50 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: The Lauberhorn descent can be demanding — assess family ski levels honestly before attempting steeper sections. The Männlichen Royal Walk is flat and safe but can be icy — wear ski boots carefully or bring microspikes if not skiing. Check the Jungfrau Region ski map app for real-time piste and lift status.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride day trip. Depart Grindelwald by regional train to Interlaken Ost, then connect toward Andermatt or board a scenic segment of the Glacier Express route. The classic Glacier Express runs between Zermatt and St. Moritz, but families can experience the most dramatic alpine scenery on the Andermatt–Disentis or Brig–Zermatt segments as a round-trip day excursion. Alternatively, take the Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' train from Kleine Scheidegg (a shorter but equally spectacular mountain railway experience) — at 3,454m, it's one of Europe's great railway journeys and highly recommended for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: If taking the Jungfraujoch route: explore the Ice Palace (carved inside the glacier), the Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and the Snow Fun Park where children can try snow tubing and zip lines. Allow 3–4 hours on the summit. Return to Grindelwald by 16:30. If taking the Glacier Express segment: enjoy the panoramic windows, dramatic viaducts, and gorge scenery before returning to Grindelwald by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in the village — browse local souvenir shops for Swiss chocolate, watches, and alpine gifts. Enjoy a relaxed dinner with the family.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet — eat well before a big travel day.
meals.lunch: Jungfraujoch Self-Service Restaurant (if taking Top of Europe route) — try the famous 'Top of Europe' lunch buffet or hot soup with bread at altitude (~CHF 20–30 per person). Or bring snacks to save costs.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Grindelwald — a family-friendly option offering wood-fired pizzas, pasta, and Swiss dishes at mid-range prices. Budget ~CHF 25–40 per adult.

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch excursion requires an additional train ticket (~CHF 145–165 per adult, ~CHF 75–85 per child — check for Swiss Travel Pass discounts). Book tickets in advance online at jungfrau.ch. Altitude sickness can affect some visitors at 3,454m — take it slowly, stay hydrated, and descend if anyone feels unwell. Bring an extra warm layer as summit temperatures can be -15°C or colder even in sunshine.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on a classic Swiss run — the Grindelwald area offers excellent family toboggan runs. Take the First gondola and sled down the Grindelwald-First toboggan run (approximately 15km — one of the longest in the Bernese Oberland). Sleds are available to rent at the top station (~CHF 10–15 per sled). The run winds through pine forests and open snowfields and is suitable for children aged 5+ when accompanied by adults. Allow 2–3 hours for multiple descents.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final ski session — use remaining lift pass validity to enjoy favorite runs once more. Focus on the Grindelwald-First area for a relaxed, unhurried afternoon of skiing. Alternatively, take a scenic horse-drawn sleigh ride through the Grindelwald valley floor — a magical and uniquely Swiss family experience (~CHF 25–40 per person for a 30-minute ride, bookable through the tourist office).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell celebration dinner at one of Grindelwald's finest mid-range restaurants. Dress slightly smartly and celebrate a wonderful week in the Alps together.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast buffet.
meals.lunch: Bergrestaurant First — enjoy a well-earned lunch at the top of the First gondola with panoramic mountain views. Try the homemade Älplermagronen or a warming goulash soup. Budget ~CHF 22–32 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Schmitte in Grindelwald — a charming converted blacksmith's workshop serving elevated Swiss cuisine including venison, lake fish, and seasonal alpine dishes. Excellent wine list. Budget ~CHF 45–65 per adult — a special splurge for the farewell evening.

day_by_day.notes: Return ski rentals by 17:00 to avoid late return fees. Tobogganing is exhilarating but ensure children wear helmets (available at rental shops). The horse-drawn sleigh ride should be booked by 10:00 AM on the day or the evening before — very popular with families. Begin packing this evening for an easier departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in Grindelwald. Enjoy a slow hotel breakfast and take one last walk through the village to soak in the alpine atmosphere. Visit the Grindelwald Museum (small local heritage museum, ~CHF 5–8 entry) for a quick insight into traditional alpine life, or simply sit at a café terrace with a coffee and admire the Eiger one last time. Do a final souvenir shop — Läderach chocolate, Lindt, Swiss army knives, and local cheese make wonderful gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the hotel by 11:00 (confirm late checkout option if your flight allows). Travel by train from Grindelwald to Interlaken Ost, then connect to Zurich HB or Geneva Cornavin depending on your departure airport. The journey takes approximately 2.5–3 hours. Allow ample time for airport check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. Reflect on an incredible week of skiing, alpine scenery, Swiss culture, and family memories in one of the world's most beautiful mountain destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast buffet — enjoy it fully!
meals.lunch: Train station lunch in Interlaken or Zurich/Geneva airport — try a Brezel, Swiss Birchermüesli yogurt pot, or a warm panini from a station café. Budget ~CHF 12–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on-board flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains are punctual and reliable — check sbb.ch for exact departure times the evening before. Grindelwald station to Interlaken Ost takes approximately 35 minutes. Allow at least 2.5 hours from Interlaken to Zurich Airport and 3 hours to Geneva Airport. Swiss customs allows bringing home up to 1kg of meat products and unlimited chocolate — stock up! Consider purchasing a Swiss chocolate assortment at the Grindelwald Coop for a fraction of airport prices.

experiences.name: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride
experiences.description: Board the legendary Glacier Express for a panoramic journey through dramatic alpine landscapes, frozen valleys, and snow-capped peaks. This family-friendly rail experience covers stunning viaducts and tunnels, offering an unforgettable window into the Swiss Alps without strenuous physical activity.

experiences.name: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking
experiences.description: Explore serene snow-covered forests and alpine meadows on a guided family snowshoeing tour. Trails are designed for all ages and fitness levels, with guides sharing local wildlife knowledge and mountain ecology. A magical way to experience the quieter side of the Alps away from ski crowds.

experiences.name: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience
experiences.description: Participate in a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class at a traditional alpine chalet, learning about centuries-old Swiss cheese-making traditions. Families enjoy melting local Gruyère and Emmental cheeses while tasting regional breads, meats, and Swiss wines or hot chocolate for kids.

experiences.name: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run
experiences.description: Experience one of Switzerland's most thrilling family-friendly toboggan runs, descending through pine forests and open alpine terrain on traditional wooden sleds. The run is well-lit for evening sessions and suitable for children aged 5 and up, making it a highlight activity for families seeking fun winter thrills.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Grindelwald-Wengen boutique accommodation via private luxury transfer (pre-arranged chauffeured Mercedes V-Class or similar). Enjoy the scenic alpine drive through the Bernese Oberland as you approach the Jungfrau Region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen (estimated arrival 15:00–15:30). After settling in, take a leisurely orientation stroll through Grindelwald village — browse the charming alpine shops, pick up any last-minute ski essentials at a premium outfitter, and enjoy the stunning views of the Eiger North Face. Visit the hotel concierge to confirm ski passes, equipment rentals, and activity bookings for the week.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at Restaurant Memories (Grand Hotel Regina, Grindelwald) — a Michelin-recognized fine dining experience featuring modern alpine cuisine with panoramic mountain views. Toast to the trip with a glass of Swiss Chasselas white wine. Early night recommended to acclimatize and rest before a full ski day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or airport)
meals.lunch: Light meal at Zurich Airport or during transfer — recommend Zurich Airport's Clouds Restaurant (airside) or a packed premium picnic box arranged by the transfer service
meals.dinner: Restaurant Memories at Grand Hotel Regina, Grindelwald — 4-course alpine tasting menu with wine pairing (approx. CHF 180–220 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer from Zurich (ZRH) or Geneva (GVA) — confirm which airport with airline. Journey time is approximately 2.5–3 hours by private car. Alternatively, upgrade to first-class rail via Interlaken Ost and Grindelwald terminal. Ensure ski equipment rental is pre-booked at a top outfitter such as Buri Sport or Intersport Grindelwald to avoid queues on Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day skiing on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — begin with a private family ski guide meeting at 09:00 at the First gondola or Männlichen cable car base station. Start on the Männlichen plateau for sweeping Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau views. The guide will assess all family members' skill levels and tailor runs accordingly across the 213km of groomed pistes. Beginners can enjoy gentle blue runs while advanced skiers tackle the challenging reds and blacks off Kleine Scheidegg.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing after a mountain lunch break. Head toward Kleine Scheidegg and explore the runs connecting to Wengen side. Advanced family members can try the iconic Lauberhorn descent (partial sections). Around 14:30, take a scenic gondola ride to enjoy the views even if taking a ski break. Wrap up skiing by 16:00 and return equipment or store at the slope-side locker.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski drinks at the Grindelwald Terminal or C and M Bar at the Belvedere Hotel — enjoy hot glühwein, Swiss craft beers, and light canapés in a lively but refined atmosphere. Dinner at Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvedere's fine dining restaurant, featuring premium Swiss and European cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss alpine breakfast at the boutique hotel — freshly baked breads, local cheeses, cold cuts, bircher muesli, fresh juices, and hot beverages (included with stay)
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Restaurant Grindelwaldblick or Bergrestaurant Männlichen — panoramic terrace dining with rösti, alpine soups, and warm fondue (approx. CHF 60–80 per person)
meals.dinner: Steigenberger Grandhotel Belvedere Restaurant, Grindelwald — seasonal alpine menu with premium Swiss beef, lake fish, and artisan cheese board (approx. CHF 150–190 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Jungfrau Ski Region Top Ski Pass (multi-day) for the family — covers all lifts across Grindelwald, Wengen, Mürren, and Kleine Scheidegg. Book a certified SWISS SNOWSPORTS private ski instructor/guide for the family at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Helmets and high-performance ski gear available at Buri Sport Grindelwald.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Express Scenic Train Ride — depart Grindelwald early (07:30) by private transfer to Zermatt or St. Moritz to board the legendary Glacier Express. Opt for the Excellence Class (the most premium cabin with panoramic windows, exclusive lounge seating, and a dedicated host). The journey winds through 291 bridges, 91 tunnels, and dramatic frozen alpine landscapes including the Oberalp Pass. This is a full-day excursion — pack warm layers and cameras.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy the Excellence Class 3-course lunch served at your panoramic seat as the train glides through the dramatic Rhône Valley and Surselva gorges. Arrive at the destination (St. Moritz or Zermatt depending on chosen direction) mid-afternoon for a brief explore of the resort town before the return journey or overnight option. Alternatively, book a one-way ticket and return via private luxury transfer for flexibility.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald-Wengen by private transfer (or first-class train via Interlaken). Relaxed evening — enjoy the hotel spa facilities (sauna, steam room, hot tub) to recover from travel. Light dinner at the hotel's in-house restaurant or a cozy local alpine restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast (request 07:00 service the evening prior) — continental spread with hot options
meals.lunch: Glacier Express Excellence Class 3-course gourmet lunch served on board — regional Swiss specialties paired with Swiss wines (included in Excellence Class fare, approx. CHF 150 supplement per person for Excellence Class upgrade)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Alte Post, Grindelwald — intimate, rustic-luxury alpine dining with fondue, raclette, and local game dishes in a 200-year-old historic building (approx. CHF 100–140 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Glacier Express Excellence Class must be booked well in advance — contact the hotel concierge immediately upon arrival to confirm availability. The full Zermatt–St. Moritz route takes approximately 8 hours; a shorter segment can be arranged for families with younger children. Ensure children have window seats — the scenery is the highlight. Bring snacks and entertainment for younger family members during longer tunnel sections.

day_by_day.morning: Family Snowshoeing and Winter Hiking guided tour — meet your certified mountain guide at 09:30 at the hotel entrance. Set off on a curated family-friendly snowshoeing route through the pristine snow-covered forests above Grindelwald toward First or the Bachalpsee lake area. The guide narrates local alpine ecology, points out winter wildlife tracks, and ensures a safe, magical experience. Snowshoe rental and poles provided; all trails are graded suitable for families.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from snowshoeing (approx. 13:00), enjoy a warm lunch at a mountain hut. Spend the afternoon at leisure — families may choose to revisit the ski slopes for a relaxed half-day of skiing, or explore the Grindelwald village ice rink (Sportzentrum Grindelwald) for ice skating, curling, and family fun in a covered premium facility.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — attend a hands-on fondue and raclette cooking class at a traditional alpine chalet starting at 18:30. Learn the art of preparing authentic Swiss fondue (Gruyère and Emmental blend), raclette, and accompaniments from a local Swiss chef. Enjoy your creations as dinner in a warm, candlelit chalet setting with local wines.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — hot buffet with eggs cooked to order, pastries, alpine honey, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch at Berghaus Bort or First Lodge — hearty alpine soup, homemade bread, and warm drinks by the fire (approx. CHF 50–70 per person)
meals.dinner: Swiss Cheese and Fondue Cultural Experience — all-inclusive cooking class and dinner with wine (approx. CHF 120–160 per person; book through hotel concierge or local operator Erlebnisschmiede)

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe tour duration is approximately 2.5–3 hours at a leisurely family pace. Waterproof, insulated boots are essential — the hotel can arrange premium rental gear if needed. The fondue cooking class is an excellent bonding experience for families and highly memorable; book at least 2–3 days in advance as evening slots fill quickly in peak February ski season. Children typically love the interactive cooking element.

day_by_day.morning: Second full ski day on Jungfrau Ski Region Slopes — this time explore the Mürren–Schilthorn side of the region. Take the Grindelwald–Lauterbrunnen–Mürren route (scenic train and cable car combination, approx. 45 min from Grindelwald). Ski the Schilthorn area with its legendary 'Bond World 007' connections and dramatic views over four countries on a clear day. The Mürren ski area offers excellent uncrowded pistes and is particularly well-suited for intermediate and advanced family skiers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Piz Gloria revolving restaurant at the top of the Schilthorn (2,970m) for lunch and the famous 007 James Bond experience (filming location of 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service'). Continue afternoon skiing on the Mürren side, enjoying the quieter, more exclusive atmosphere compared to busier Grindelwald slopes. Head back to Grindelwald by 16:30 via cable car and train.
day_by_day.evening: Spa and wellness evening at the hotel — enjoy the full spa circuit including heated outdoor pool (if available), sauna, steam room, and a booked couples or family massage treatment. Dinner at a sophisticated but relaxed restaurant in Grindelwald.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast with made-to-order omelette station and freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Piz Gloria Revolving Restaurant, Schilthorn summit — panoramic 360° dining experience with classic Swiss and international dishes; the views over the Bernese Alps are unparalleled (approx. CHF 70–100 per person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestarter, Grindelwald — premium mountain grill restaurant featuring premium Swiss beef, local lamb, and seasonal alpine vegetables with an extensive Swiss wine list (approx. CHF 120–160 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Schilthorn excursion requires departing Grindelwald by 08:30 to maximize skiing time. The Piz Gloria restaurant requires reservations — book through the hotel concierge at least 2 days prior. On clear days, visibility from the Schilthorn extends to the French Alps and Black Forest — check weather forecasts the evening before. The Bond World 007 interactive museum at the summit is free with lift ticket and is a big hit with children and adults alike.

day_by_day.morning: Tobogganing on the Fläsch-Maienfeld Run — depart hotel by private transfer at 08:30 to reach the Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan run in the Rhine Valley (approximately 1.5 hours drive). This is one of Switzerland's most thrilling and scenic family-friendly toboggan runs, descending through pine forests with stunning valley views. Premium wooden sleds are available for hire at the top. Multiple runs can be completed in the morning session — guides accompany the family for safety and maximum fun.
day_by_day.afternoon: After tobogganing, stop for lunch in the charming wine village of Maienfeld (inspiration for Heidi's village) — explore the Heidi House museum, a delightful cultural stop particularly loved by younger family members. Browse the local artisan shops before the private transfer back to Grindelwald (arriving approximately 15:30). Spend the remaining afternoon at leisure — last-minute souvenir shopping in Grindelwald village or a relaxed walk along the valley floor.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at one of Grindelwald's most prestigious restaurants — reserve the private dining room at The Eiger Boutique Hotel's restaurant or Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof for a special celebration dinner. Enjoy a 5-course tasting menu with Swiss wine pairing, reflecting on a spectacular week in the Alps.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast at 07:30 (request the night before) — full hot and cold spread
meals.lunch: Traditional Swiss lunch in Maienfeld village — Restaurant Zum Rebstock or a local Wirtschaft (inn) serving regional specialties including Bündner Gerstensuppe (barley soup), local charcuterie, and Maienfeld wines (approx. CHF 60–80 per person)
meals.dinner: Farewell 5-course tasting dinner at Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof or The Eiger Restaurant, Grindelwald — premium Swiss seasonal menu with curated wine pairing (approx. CHF 200–280 per person; reserve private dining room for the family)

day_by_day.notes: The Fläsch-Maienfeld toboggan run is approximately 1.5 hours from Grindelwald — confirm road conditions and transfer logistics with the hotel concierge the evening prior. The Heidi House in Maienfeld (Heididorf) is open year-round and is a wonderful cultural detour, especially for families with children aged 4–12. Ensure the farewell dinner reservation is made at the start of the trip as Saturday evenings in peak season book up very quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — enjoy a long, relaxed hotel breakfast savoring the last views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau from the dining room. Depending on checkout time, take one final short walk through Grindelwald village or ride the gondola to First for a farewell view of the entire Jungfrau ski region. Collect any stored ski equipment and return rentals before 10:00 to avoid late fees.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel (standard checkout 11:00 — request late checkout until 13:00 if needed, subject to availability). Private luxury transfer departs for Zurich Airport (ZRH) or Geneva Airport (GVA) at 12:00–13:00 depending on flight schedule. The scenic drive through the Bernese Oberland and Swiss Mittelland provides a beautiful final impression of Switzerland. Allow 2.5–3 hours transfer time plus 2 hours airport check-in buffer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — fly home with extraordinary memories of a world-class Swiss Alps family adventure.

meals.breakfast: Final full hotel breakfast — order à la carte specials such as truffle scrambled eggs, smoked salmon, and Swiss pastry basket as a special send-off treat
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel (request a packed premium picnic or charcuterie box for the transfer journey) or dine at Zurich Airport's top-tier restaurants airside (The Circle at ZRH offers excellent dining options pre-departure)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight dining (request premium meal pre-selection with airline)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer booking at least 24 hours before departure. Tip the hotel concierge team generously — their assistance throughout the week is invaluable for a seamless luxury experience. Request the hotel to arrange gift wrapping for any local purchases (Swiss chocolates, watches, alpine souvenirs). Consider purchasing a selection of Swiss artisan products — Läderach chocolates, Gruyère cheese to travel, and a bottle of Swiss wine — as gifts or mementos. Ensure all ski passes are returned if deposit-based.
